summary: Constellation Safety & Integrity Audit — adversarial hunt for silent app-killer bugs (whole-app or diff-scoped)

confirmed_findings.summary: Every rename/move/create write-path tail resolves its reindex library through load_all_libraries (the FEDERATED recursive resolver) instead of the own-library loader, so touching a linked universe's note silently adopts it into the ACTIVE universe's index — the exact class PJ-207 §8 closed at six other surfaces.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: libraries.rs:266-269 states the contract in the file itself: an attribution resolver that 'feeds a write or a reindex' MUST use load_libraries (own, non-recursive) and NEVER load_all_libraries, 'because a write must never target a read-only cUniverse note (MIG-065 §J)'. reindex_changed_paths (search.rs:12934) obeys it via try_load_libraries. These do not: rename_item_db_tail (libraries.rs:1774 load_all_libraries → 1776 library_name_for_path), rename_folder_db_tail (1805 → 1849), move_item_db_tail (2614 → 2654), create_note (1334), update_links_on_rename's detached reindex (6870 → 6873). Concrete run: the active Universe federates a cUniverse; store.ts:3845 populates the sidebar from resolve_universe_libraries, so the child universe's library and its notes are on screen; validate_path_in_any_library (653) authorizes against the federated set, so the note is renameable. User renames it. gate_rmw_rename succeeds, the tail runs, library_name_for_path over the FEDERATED list returns the FOREIGN library name (never None), and reindex_single_note → index_note_impl (search.rs:7848) has no ownership guard at all — it indexes whatever path+library the caller hands it. A row for another universe's note is now written into this universe's note_meta/notes_fts/note_links/sky_links. The gated rename suppressed the watcher, so nothing heals it; the child universe's own index still points at the pre-rename path. Renaming a plain SUBFOLDER inside a foreign library is worse: guard_no_foreign_library_under (1592) only refuses folders that ARE or CONTAIN a registered library, so a subfolder passes and rename_folder_db_tail adopts every descendant in one pass. Zero errors, zero UI signal — the adoption is only visible by querying note_meta, which is how §8's original 13 rows were found.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at the code, and reachable by an ordinary gesture. (1) The sidebar's library list IS the federated set — store.ts:3841 invokes resolve_universe_libraries (universe.rs:1503 → resolve_libraries_recursive), +layout.svelte:6918/6832 render and expand cUniverse libraries, LibraryInfo (libraries.rs:6) has no read-only flag, FileTree.svelte gates rename on nothing, and handleRenameComplete (+layout.svelte:7247) has no scope check. rename_item authorizes via validate_path_in_any_library (libraries.rs:653), which loops load_all_libraries — federated included — so a linked universe's note is renameable. (2) The tail then adopts it: libraries.rs:1774 load_all_libraries → 1776 library_name_for_path returns the FOREIGN library name (never None) → reindex_single_note → index_note_impl (search.rs:7848), which has no ownership guard at all and upserts note_meta/notes_fts/note_links/sky_links into the ACTIVE universe's search.db (per-universe: db_path, search.rs:1465). Identical shape at rename_folder_db_tail (1805/1849 — guard_no_foreign_library_under only refuses folders that ARE or CONTAIN a registered library, so a plain subfolder inside a foreign library adopts every descendant in one pass), move_item_db_tail (2614/2654) and create_note (1334). This is the exact rule the file states at libraries.rs:266-269 and search.rs:11970-11980 ("it reaches this one through the federated ATTACH search path, not by being copied in"). (3) Nothing heals it and nothing says it: reconcile.rs:344-357 deliberately SKIPS healing out-of-root rows (the `continue` is annotated load-bearing) and only counts them as DriftReport.foreign_rows; driftReport.ts:58 hasFindings deliberately excludes foreignRows (§13 unshipped) and foreignRows is referenced nowhere else in src/, so no band renders; the gated rename suppresses the watcher, and reindex_changed_paths (search.rs:12934) is already scoped to try_load_libraries so it can never remove the row. The tail logs "[rename-tail] reindex OK" — it reads as success. (4) The §8 wiring guard (index_repair.rs:1294) whitelists only reconcile.rs / index_repair.rs / library_attribution_backfill.rs plus two search.rs functions, so libraries.rs is outside its file list and the suite stays green. One partial refutation: the cascade reindex at libraries.rs:6870 is benign in practice — update_links_recursive already excludes foreign roots, so result.rewritten holds only own-universe paths; that site is latent drift, not a live defect. Not an app-killer: the .md files are untouched and the child universe's own index self-heals on its next boot (stale row + orphan matched by cid_cn). The durable damage is silent, unhealable index divergence in the active universe — Charter W2-9, the class PJ-207 §8 closed at six other surfaces and missed here.

confirmed_findings.summary: `moveItem` repaths the open tab and its model but never re-resolves `t.libraryName`, so after a CROSS-LIBRARY move every subsequent save reindexes the note under the SOURCE library and silently refiles its note_meta / note_links / sky_nodes rows.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note `X.md` lives in Library A and is open in a tab (`tab.libraryName === 'A'`). The user picks Move to… and chooses a folder inside Library B (`handleMoveConfirm`, +layout.svelte:6993, explicitly supports `targetLibId !== libraryId`). Rust `move_item_db_tail` (libraries.rs:2655) correctly reindexes the new path with `library_name_for_path` → note_meta.library_name = 'B'. Back in JS, `openTabs.update` at store.ts:4918-4923 rewrites `path` and `name` and calls `repathNoteModel`, but spreads `...t` — `libraryName` stays 'A'. (`loadTabHistoryEntry` does re-resolve it via `deriveLibraryForPath` at store.ts:2059-2073, with the comment "cross-library history entries … don't keep the old library's name/path on the tab" — moveItem is the sibling that never got it.) The user then types one character in the still-open tab; the 1500 ms debounce fires `handleSave` → `onSaved` → `reindexNote(savedPath, tab.libraryName /* 'A' */)` (NoteEditor.svelte:322). `index_note_impl`'s UPSERT sets `library_name = excluded.library_name` (search.rs:8136), the note_links rows are rebuilt with `library_name = 'A'` (search.rs:8534), and the note_meta AU trigger (`OR OLD.library_name IS NOT NEW.library_name`, search.rs:5685/5702) rewrites sky_nodes.library_name to 'A'. The note now physically lives in Library B while every library-scoped surface (per-library star/note counts, library-filtered search `library_names`, Sky View per library, link scoping) claims Library A. No error is raised, the save reports success, boot never re-walks an indexed library, and the app's own write is watcher-suppressed — nothing heals it. Same bug via OrgChart drag-move (OrgChart.svelte:262) and the batch move loop (+layout.svelte:6979).
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified end-to-end in source. (1) Cross-library move is a live, intended flow: handleMoveConfirm (+layout.svelte:6992-7010) branches on targetLibId !== libraryId and the picker is universe-wide (list_universe_folders, libraries.rs:2720); the batch loop (+layout.svelte:6979) shares it. (2) moveItem (store.ts:4918-4923) spreads ...t and rewrites only path/name — libraryName (and libraryPath) stay at the SOURCE library. deriveLibraryForPath exists and is called by all three sibling repath sites (store.ts:2060 history nav, 3216 openNoteTab, 3697 restoreTabs); moveItem is the one that needs it most and never calls it. (3) Rust move_item_db_tail (libraries.rs:2654) correctly reindexes to library B via library_name_for_path — then the next debounced save from the still-open tab calls reindexNote(savedPath, tab.libraryName='A') (NoteEditor.svelte:322) → constellation_search_reindex (search.rs:12215) → reindex_single_note → index_note(force=true) (search.rs:12682, 7837), whose UPSERT sets library_name = excluded.library_name (search.rs:8129-8135), rebuilds note_links with library_name (search.rs:8533/8547), and fires note_meta_sky_au on OLD.library_name IS NOT NEW.library_name (search.rs:5685) to rewrite sky_nodes.library_name. force=true bypasses the mtime gate, so it is unconditional. (4) Refutation attempts all fail: the app's own save is watcher-suppressed on BOTH sides (wasRecentlyWritten gates pendingReindex at +layout.svelte:3750-3754; write_gate.rs:256-257 marks watcher_suppress), so reindex_changed_paths — which WOULD have re-resolved correctly (search.rs:12973) — never sees the path; library_attribution_backfill is a version-stamped one-off (LIB_ATTR_VERSION=1, is_needed false once stamped) and does not re-run; boot never re-walks an indexed library and index_note's mtime gate would block it; reindexNote's indexHealthError only surfaces REJECTIONS and this call succeeds, so no error is raised anywhere. Only a manual Settings → Index → Repair index (index_repair.rs:851) heals it, with nothing prompting the user. (5) The wrong value has real consumers: library-scoped search filter (search.rs:9546 library_name IN (...)), tension.rs:241/281/308 per-library analyses, index_repair.rs:807 per-library counts, and sky_nodes attribution — the same shape the project already fixed once with a dedicated backfill ("nested library reported 0 notes", library_attribution_backfill.rs:1-10). Two corrections to the candidate: the OrgChart drag site (OrgChart.svelte:262) is documented in-file as currently unreachable (latent, not a live vector), and tab.libraryPath is stale by the same root cause, widening the concern beyond reindex.

confirmed_findings.summary: openNoteTab's new-tab branch has no post-await one-path-one-tab re-check, so a path can end up with TWO tabs and therefore TWO independent NoteModels; the second model's save then silently overwrites the first model's edits with no conflict and no banner.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The DEDUP_ALL_TABS_ENABLED check (store.ts:3176-3188) is a single synchronous snapshot taken BEFORE two awaits — `resolveNoteContent` (3199, a read_note IPC) and `ensure_cid_cn_cmd` (3245, which can perform a gated disk WRITE). Nothing re-checks after them: lines 3405-3413 mint `tab_${++tabCounter}_...` and call `openNoteModel(id, filePath, content)` unconditionally. Its sibling `restoreSessionTabs` demonstrates the correct shape — it re-dedups INSIDE the commit (`const have = new Set(ts.map(t => t.path)); appended = built.filter(b => !have.has(b.path))`, 3720-3724). Concrete recipe: at boot, `restoreSessionTabs` walks N saved tabs sequentially, each awaiting `resolveNoteContent` (session.ts:386 awaits it while the sidebar is already interactive). The user clicks note P in the file tree during that walk. At that moment `activeTabId` is still null, so `currentTab` is null and openNoteTab takes the new-tab branch; its dedup snapshot saw an empty/short tab list. While its own read is in flight, restore performs its single `openTabs.update` and appends its tab for P with `openNoteModel(t.id, ...)`. openNoteTab then resumes and appends a SECOND tab for P with a SECOND model. Both models hold P; `noteSession.saveChains` serialises per MODEL ID, not per path, so they do not serialise against each other. The user edits in tab A and it autosaves (disk = A's content, A's diskBaseline updated). Tab B's model is untouched and still clean at its stale open-time content; `write_note` is watcher-suppressed and `markRecentWrite` gates the rest, so B never receives an external-change event and `adoptDisk` never runs. The user later types one character in tab B; B composes from its stale base and durably writes, erasing A's paragraphs. `markSaved` reports clean, `clearWriteAheadIf` clears the net, no `.conflict` sidecar is written (that branch only fires from `adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs`, which never saw an event), and no save-health row appears. In split view both duplicate tabs render side by side (+layout.svelte:9186 renders a NoteEditor per open tab), so both are simultaneously editable and the clobber is a normal editing gesture rather than a race the user can perceive.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified by reading the code, not inferred. (1) The one-path-one-tab guard at store.ts:3176-3188 is a single synchronous get(openTabs) snapshot taken BEFORE two awaits (resolveNoteContent 3199, ensure_cid_cn_cmd 3245). The reuse branch received a post-await liveness re-check (3353-3357) but the new-tab branch at 3405-3413 appends the tab and calls openNoteModel(id,…) unconditionally. The sibling restoreSessionTabs proves the correct shape — it re-dedups INSIDE the commit (3716-3724, `const have = new Set(ts.map(t=>t.path)); appended = built.filter(b=>!have.has(b.path))`). loadTabHistoryEntry's own comment (2006-2008) already concedes the identical residual. (2) Nothing downstream collapses a duplicate: noteModel.openModel (noteModel.ts:189-221) keys models by tab id with NO path-ownership registry; noteSession saveChains (noteSession.ts:206-242) serialise per id, not per path; NoteEditor's ensureModel(tab.id, tab.path, tab.content) (NoteEditor.svelte:189) deliberately leaves an existing same-path model untouched, so the stale twin is never re-seeded. (3) The write is unchecked: standardSaveEnv.write → writeNote(p,c,origin) (store.ts:2837-2842) passes no `expect` attestation, so write_gate (libraries.rs:889-936) overwrites without a freshness check. (4) No self-heal: frontend gated writes are watcher-suppressed and write_note never announces — announce_disk_write exists only for template merge (universe.rs:2639) — so the twin's clean model receives no library-changed event, adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs never runs on it, and the .conflict sidecar (its only trigger) never fires. adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs even records the now-false assumption "path↔id is 1:1 under DEDUP" (store.ts:1320). (5) Reachable: session restore is fire-and-forget after paint while the UI is live (+layout.svelte:2921-2938) and awaits resolveNoteContent per saved tab sequentially; during that loop activeTabId is null so currentTab is null and a click on the home recent-notes list or the file tree (newTab=false, +layout.svelte:7623) takes the NEW-TAB branch. read_note is a sync Tauri command (libraries.rs:851) so the two flows interleave on one dispatch queue; when restore's single commit lands inside the click's IPC window both append, yielding two tabs and two independent NoteModels for one path. (6) Worse in split view: +layout.svelte:9186-9210 renders a NoteEditor per open tab under {#each $openTabs}, so both duplicates mount live editors on the same file at once; the later writer composes from its stale base and durably erases the other's saved paragraphs while markSaved reports clean, clearWriteAheadIf clears the net, and no banner, sidecar or save-health row appears. Not refutable by any guard, version gate, trigger, reconcile or onDestroy cleanup on this path. Held below APP-KILLER only by reachability: it requires a millisecond-scale interleaving of two same-path opens that both reach the new-tab branch, not a routine gesture. Fix shape is already in-repo: move the dedup into the openTabs.update commit, exactly as restoreSessionTabs does (and normalise with normPath on both sides, which restoreSessionTabs currently does not).

confirmed_findings.summary: In the right-sidebar Properties panel (an unkeyed, surviving instance), `|| tabChanged` overrides the `localEditPending` guard, so a tab switch re-seeds `editableProps` from the incoming note and silently discards the outgoing note's un-committed property edit.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The sidebar mount (+layout.svelte:9731, `tabId={sidebarTab.id}` where `sidebarTab = $derived($focusedTab)` at :1631) is NOT wrapped in a `{#key}` — the component instance survives a tab switch and only its props change, so there is no onDestroy flush at all. Scenario: with notes A and B open, the user types a value into a property row in the right sidebar for note A and, within the 800 ms debounce, clicks note B's tab. `sidebarTab` changes → the seed `$effect` re-runs → `tabChanged` is true → line 457 `if ((!saving && !localEditPending) || tabChanged)` takes the re-seed branch despite `localEditPending`, setting `seededForPath = filePath` (B), `seededRows`/`editableProps` = B's rows (:458-493). A's typed value is overwritten in memory. The still-armed `saveTimeout` then fires `commitAndSave(tabId, filePath)` with B's identity; `rowsBelongToTarget` passes (rows are B's), `touchedSince(seededRows, localRows)` finds nothing touched, `if (!changed && !isNoteDirty(id)) return` (:1047) — nothing is written. Note A's frontmatter edit is gone from the panel, never reached A's model, never reached A's .md, no write-ahead net, no error, no console warning. The code comment at :454-455 asserts 'its pending edit is flushed by the teardown path' — true only for the embedded instance inside the `{#key}`, false for this surviving sidebar instance.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source, not inferred. The right-sidebar mount (+layout.svelte:9726-9748) sits inside a plain {#if rightSidebarTab === 'properties' && sidebarTab} with tabId/filePath as props, NO {#key} and no bind:this; focusedTab (store.ts:1950) never goes null between two open tabs, so the condition stays truthy and the PropertyEditor instance survives a tab switch — onDestroy never runs, so the teardown flush at :604-641 never fires. updateValue (:715) writes ONLY local editableProps and arms the 800 ms debounce; grep confirms editPropValue/addPropTo/removePropFrom are reachable only from commitAndSave (:1020-1025), so a keystroke never reaches the note model, and the model-level navigation flushes (flushOpenTabOrAbort, gated on isNoteDirty) therefore cannot see it. There is no onblur/onfocusout in the component and the only exports are addProperty/removeProperty (:728,:732), so no caller can flush it either. Concrete reachable path: with notes A and B open and the right sidebar on Properties, type a value into a property row for A and click B's tab within 800 ms. sidebarTab changes -> the seed $effect (:442) re-runs -> tabChanged is true -> line 457 `if ((!saving && !localEditPending) || tabChanged)` takes the re-seed branch despite localEditPending, setting seededForPath = B's path and overwriting seededRows/editableProps with B's rows (:458-497). A's typed value is destroyed in memory. The still-armed timer then calls commitAndSave(tabId, filePath) with the LIVE (B) identity: rowsBelongToTarget(B, B) passes (:991), touchedSince over B-vs-B finds nothing, and `if (!changed && !isNoteDirty(id)) return` (:1047) exits — nothing is written for A. Net result: the edit never reached A's model, never reached A's .md, produced no error, no console warning, no write-ahead record; the panel now displays B so the user sees no cue. The comment at :454-455 ("its pending edit is flushed by the teardown path") is false for this surviving instance, and the component itself concedes the gap at :988-990 ("flushing pending PANEL edits at navigation time ... — filed") — filed is not guarded. Secondary confirmed effect: the post-switch commit runs withAutoUpdatedDate (store.ts:1771) over B's rows, so if B carries an updated/modified date property it is bumped and written to B's .md although the user never edited B. No guard refutes it: the PJ-187 rowsBelongToTarget guard is satisfied (rows were re-seeded to B), no version gate/trigger/reconcile touches un-modelled panel state, and nothing self-corrects visibly. Severity HIGH rather than APP-KILLER: nothing already persisted in A is corrupted or deleted; the blast radius is the single un-flushed panel edit (which can be an entire typed value, since the debounce re-arms on every keystroke).

confirmed_findings.summary: restashConsumedNet re-stashes a consumed write-ahead entry WITHOUT its PJ-181 `snapshot` flag, converting a harmless "already durable on disk" view-stash into an entry that claims to be real unsaved work — which then outranks a newer file on the next open and is written over it.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: setWriteAhead's 5th arg is passed at exactly one site (NoteEditor.svelte:427); the three restash sites (store.ts:2036, 2087, 3227) all omit it. Sequence: (1) user views note A and closes/leaves it — NoteEditor's teardown stashes entry E = {content C, snapshot:true} (localStorage `constellation-wab`), which is the ordinary case per store.ts:3065 ("merely VIEWING a note leaves one of these, nothing clears it for a closed note"). (2) Later the user presses Alt+← twice quickly, or clicks note A while the outgoing tab's flush fails on a locked .md: resolveNoteContent(A) hits E, identity is proven, staleSnapshot is false (disk still == C), so it returns recoveredFromNet:true and CLEARS the entry (store.ts:3109); the nav then aborts (`_navTokens` supersede at store.ts:2040/2048, flush abort at 3343, or tab-closed at 3353) and calls restashConsumedNet → setWriteAhead(A, C, …) with no snapshot flag. E is now {content C} — indistinguishable from a failed-save recovery copy. (3) Syncthing / another device / `git pull` rewrites A on disk to C'. cid_cn is unchanged by an edit, so identityProven still passes. (4) User opens A: staleSnapshot is now FALSE (the flag is gone), so the PJ-181 rejection at store.ts:3077 does not fire; the net wins the screen, markModelRecoveredFromNet births the model DIRTY with baseline C' (store.ts:3395), and the first debounced save / departure flush durably writes the stale C over C'. The externally-added text is gone from screen and disk, with no banner, no conflict sidecar and no journal anomaly — this is the exact PJ-181 app-killer shape, re-entered through the restash side door.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source. setWriteAhead (store.ts:340-352) builds a snapshot-flagged entry only when the 5th arg is passed; the sole caller passing it is NoteEditor.svelte:427, and all three restash closures (store.ts:2036, 2087, 3227) omit it, with a comment asserting the entry must be "real unsaved work" — an assumption that is false for a snapshot whose bytes still match disk. Concrete reachable failure: (1) user views note A and leaves it — NoteEditor.svelte:427 stashes {C, snapshot:true} (needsDiskSave false, model clean). (2) User types in note B (model dirty) while a rename cascade is running or a sync agent/AV holds B's .md; user clicks A. resolveNoteContent(A) hits the wab, disk still == C so staleSnapshot (store.ts:3076) is false and identityProven passes, so it consumes the entry at :3109 and returns recoveredFromNet:true. flushOutgoing(B) then returns {ok:false} — via the isCascading refusal at store.ts:709 or write_failed — and openNoteTab:3343 calls restashConsumedNet → setWriteAhead(A, C, cursor, scroll) with no flag. NAV_FLUSH_ENABLED and SINGLE_OWNERSHIP are both true. The nav aborts, so A is never displayed and its entry is now {content:C}, flagless, persisted in localStorage (constellation-wab), which the code documents as never pruned or capped. (3) Syncthing/git pull rewrites A to C'; cid_cn is unchanged by an edit so identityProven still passes. No clearWriteAhead site touches a closed note on external change (store.ts:1174 is the rename-cascade adopt; :1379 and :3731 iterate openTabs only). (4) User opens A: with the flag gone staleSnapshot is false, the PJ-181 rejection at store.ts:3077 does not fire, the net wins the screen, markRecoveredFromNet (noteModel.ts:484-494) sets diskBaseline = C' and version++ so the model is born dirty. The first debounced save or departure flush runs saveUnchained (noteSession.ts:247-270), which has NO disk-vs-baseline conflict check — only path/lineage guards — so it durably writes stale C over C', markRecentWrite suppresses the watcher, and the reindex runs on the stale bytes. Return value is ok:true; no banner, no .conflict sidecar, no journal anomaly. The defect is also self-sustaining: reopening from a flagless net births the model dirty, so NoteEditor.svelte:427's !isModelDirty(tab.id) is false and the teardown re-stashes flagless again. Refutation attempts that failed: setWriteAhead's downgrade guard (:346-349) only applies when snapshot===true, so it cannot block the flagless overwrite; the save path has no baseline conflict check; the watcher/adopt reconcilers are open-tab-scoped; and the store.ts:711 restash is correctly unflagged because that content genuinely is unsaved work. The information needed for the fix is already available at the restash sites (resolved.diskContent === resolved.content).

confirmed_findings.summary: After a successful commit, `seededRows` is re-baselined from the RAW model props while `editableProps` keeps the panel's DISPLAY-transformed rows and is not re-seeded — so the next commit's `seededKeysOf(seededRows)` contains keys the panel never displayed (they become REMOVE ops) and `touchedSince` marks every type-overridden row as edited (they become spurious SET ops).
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note has `title`, `stage`, `parent: "[[Architecture]]"`. Right-sidebar Properties panel is open on the same tab as NotePane's embedded panel. (1) User edits `stage` in the sidebar → 800 ms debounce. (2) Inside that window another writer adds a key to the model — the embedded panel adds `author`, or a file-tree right-click adds `tags`, or Reviewer connect adds a typed-link key. (3) The sidebar commit fires: plan is computed against the correct seed (no damage), then line 1051 sets `seededRows = model.props` = {title, stage, parent, author}. (4) `await saveTabContent` yields; the user types one more character in any field during the disk write, so `saveTimeout` is set. (5) The seed `$effect` re-runs when `saving` flips false, sees `localEditPending`, SKIPS the re-seed — `editableProps` is still {title, stage, parent}, `seededRows` is {…, author}. (6) The next commit: `plan`'s REMOVE loop finds `author` in seededKeys, absent from localKeys, present in the model → emits `remove('author')`; the model drops it and compose splices the key out of the .md. In the same pass `parent` (whose displayed type is forced to 'list' by `structuralKeyType`, while the raw model row is type 'link') no longer matches its baseline → SET with type='list' → `serializeLine` rewrites the scalar as a block sequence on disk. Both writes report success, the reindex follows the file down, and nothing anywhere reports a discrepancy. This is the exact defect PJ-207 §15 fixed at the seed site ("the baseline has to describe what is on screen", line 492 clones the TRANSFORMED rows) and the exact loss `seededKeys` was built to make unrepresentable — reintroduced by the post-commit assignment. Worse variant: a key registered library-wide as List whose value on this note is a comma scalar (`author: Rosenthal, F.`) is re-baselined raw, counted as touched, and `listItemsOf` splits it — one author becomes two list items on disk.
confirmed_findings.reason: Line 1051 re-baselines `seededRows` from the RAW model props while `editableProps` keeps the display-transformed rows (seed site 467-493: structuralKeyType forces parent/contains to 'list', getRegisteredType applies the library type, listItemsOf derives items from a comma scalar). Nothing re-aligns them except the seed $effect (442-506), which skips whenever `saveTimeout !== undefined`; `saveTimeout` is a plain `let` (line 219), not $state, so clearing it schedules no re-run, and the only post-commit trigger is `saving = false` (1083). If any panel interaction re-arms the debounce during `await saveTabContent` (1052), that flush skips and no later trigger exists before the next commit (saving=true re-enters the same skip) — the mismatch does not self-correct. The next commit consumes it: `touchedSince` uses `samePropRow` (propRow.ts), which compares `type` AND `listItems`, so every type-overridden row is marked edited though untouched, and its second loop marks any seeded-but-absent key; `seededKeysOf(seededRows)` now holds keys the panel never displayed, so plan's REMOVE loop emits `remove(key)` for them. Nothing stops the damage reaching disk: removeProp (noteModel.ts:378) and setPropValue (319) accept it, serializeLine (yamlDoc.ts:266) emits type 'list' as a block sequence, and `apply` reports changed:true with an empty `refused` list — so no PJ-187 banner and no console error fire, and reindexNote follows the file down. Both preconditions are real. The type-divergence vector needs NO second writer: detectPropertyType (store.ts:216) types `parent: "[[X]]"` as 'link' while the panel forces 'list' — verbatim the defect the seed-site comment at 459-466 says it fixed — and a registry-'list' key holding `author: Rosenthal, F.` is split into two list items by listItemsOf. confirmed_findings.summary: note_links.target_cid_cn is never cleared when its target note is de-indexed, and the back-resolution triggers only fill NULL/empty values — so after a note is deleted and a new note is created under the same title, every pre-existing inbound link stays bound to the dead identity and the Reviewer's staleness lens silently stops seeing it.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note A contains `[[derives-from::Evidence]]`; Evidence.md carries cid C1, so A's note_links row is stamped target_cid_cn = 'C1'. The user deletes Evidence.md. reindex_delete_note (search.rs:12332) purges note_meta / note_links WHERE source_path / note_aliases / note_embeddings for the dead note, but issues no statement touching the target_cid_cn of INBOUND edges — grep of the whole crate shows target_cid_cn is written in only five places (search.rs:4425, 5646, 5749, and the index_note link-rebuild INSERTs at 8532/8544/8566), and all of the first three carry `AND (target_cid_cn IS NULL OR target_cid_cn = '')`. The user then creates a fresh Evidence.md, which gets a new cid C2. note_meta_sky_ai's back-resolution (line 5646-5649) tries to stamp every link named 'evidence' — but A's row is non-empty, so the guard at 5649 skips it. A's row still says C1. The Reviewer's Mode-2 staleness probe joins on identity (review.rs:145 stale_probe_sql: `JOIN note_meta dep ON dep.cid_cn = jl.target_cid_cn`), finds no row for C1, and A is never flagged when the new Evidence changes — a load-bearing dependency the user can see on disk in A's own text is invisible to the surface built to watch it. The only repair is A itself being re-indexed (its link rebuild recomputes target_cid_cn and, seeing o_tcc != target_cid_cn at search.rs:8511, rewrites the edge) — which happens only if the user happens to edit A, or runs a full 'Repair now'. No error, no drift notice: reconcile.rs only compares row/file existence and mtime, never link identity.

confirmed_findings.summary: `plan()`'s ADD branch is not gated by `touchedKeys` (unlike the SET branch two lines below), so a row the panel is merely displaying and the user never touched is re-ADDED when another writer has removed that key from the model — silently reverting the deletion and writing the stale value back to the .md.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note has `stage: birth`. Both Properties panels are mounted on the same tab (NotePane's embedded one and the right-sidebar one at +layout.svelte:9731). (3) The sidebar commit fires: `stage` is still in its `localRows`, is NOT in `touchedKeys` (untouched since seed), and `byModelKey.get('stage')` is now undefined → `plan` emits `{op:'add', prop:{key:'stage', value:'birth'}}`. `noteModel.addProp` accepts it (the key is absent, so its collision guard does not fire), version bumps, `saveTabContent` composes and `serializeLine` appends `stage: birth` back into the frontmatter. The user's deletion is durably undone with no error, no refusal, and no banner — `applyPropOps` reports `changed:true`, so it looks like a normal successful save. The SET branch's own comment (line 115-117) states this hazard for values ("Writing it back is how a value another writer changed gets silently reverted"); the ADD branch is the same hazard for deletions and is ungated. Gating it on `touchedKeys` is safe for genuine adds, because a key absent from `seededRows` is always in `touchedSince`'s output.

confirmed_findings.summary: `commitFocusSave` — the FocusPane save path — is the fifth durable-save site and the only one that never calls `reembedNote`, so a note edited in Focus mode keeps its pre-edit semantic vector permanently.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: With Settings → semantic search ON, the user opens a note in Focus mode and types three paragraphs. `onchange` pushes the body into the model; 1500 ms later (or on exit/onflush) `commitFocusSave` runs `saveNoteSession(..., standardSaveEnv({ origin:'focus_pane', onSaved: broadcast + reindexNote }))` — reindex only. `reembedNote` is called at exactly four sites (NoteEditor.svelte:329 editor_save, :445 editor_flush, store.ts:660 navFlushEnv, store.ts:1875 prop_save) and this is not one of them. Result: lexical search finds the new text; semantic search, "similar notes", RelatedCandidates and CECE keep answering from the paragraph the user replaced — forever, for any note the user only ever edits in Focus. `embedHealthError` is never set because the call is never made, so there is no banner, no console line, and no observable cue anywhere. confirmed_findings.summary: `retrySaveFailure`'s onSaved carries only `reindexNote` — no `reembedNote` and no `emit('screen:note-saved')` — so the one path that finally persists previously-failed content leaves the semantic index and the second screen behind.

With semantic search on, the note that was hardest to persist ends up with a vector frozen at its pre-edit text, permanently (same non-self-correcting mechanism as `reembedNote`'s own header documents); with the second screen open, that window keeps rendering the pre-retry content because it never receives the save event that drives its freshness-gated adopt. Both are silent — the banner is gone, so every visible signal says the save fully landed.
confirmed_findings.reason:

confirmed_findings.summary: `flushOpenTabOrAbort` writes the user's unsaved body durably through a BARE `standardSaveEnv` (no reindex, no embed, no second-screen broadcast), and a caller that then returns early leaves that content on disk and out of the index with nothing to re-drive it.

confirmed_findings.summary: `writeCanvasNow` clears the `saveDirty` flag after its await using no version/generation stamp, so a change made WHILE a write is in flight is marked already-durable; `flushPendingSave` then cancels that change's armed timer and skips the write.

T+1.5s: the FIRST write resolves and line 185 executes `saveDirty = false` — but card B's move is not in those bytes. T+2.0s: the user closes the app (or switches canvas / picks another canvas). The app-close handshake calls `flushPendingSave()` (registered at line 213 in `pendingCanvasFlushes`), which at line 206 clears the armed T+2.2s timer and at line 207 evaluates `if (saveDirty)` — false — and returns without writing. Card B's move is gone from disk, gone from memory, with no error, no `saveError` banner (line 367 renders only on a rejected write), and no console line. `onDestroy` (line 218) has the identical shape. The correct form is the one `noteModel`/`noteSession` already use: stamp a monotonic version at compose time and only clear the dirty flag when the version that was written is still the newest (`markSaved(id, r.version, …)` in noteSession.ts:269).

confirmed_findings.summary: `links_backfill::maybe_schedule` and `incoming_links_backfill::maybe_schedule` spawn an unguarded full-corpus backfill thread on every call — they gate only on a stamp that is written at COMPLETION, and both are re-invoked from `on_link_vocabulary_changed` (search.rs:2750 and search.rs:2756) on every link-type vocabulary edit, so N edits during one run produce N concurrent full-corpus writers.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Eisa opens Settings → Links (LinkTypesEditor.svelte) and adds three custom link types in quick succession. Each `addType()` calls `persist()` → `saveLinkTypes` → `save_universe_link_types` (link_types.rs:544), whose fingerprint check passes and calls `on_link_vocabulary_changed` (search.rs:2735). That schedules BOTH backfills. `links_backfill::maybe_schedule` (links_backfill.rs:57) gates on `is_needed()`, which reads `schema_versions.links_vocab` — only written by `finalize` at the end of a pass; `incoming_links_backfill::maybe_schedule` (incoming_links_backfill.rs:97) gates on `is_stamped()`, likewise written only at the end. On the Boss's 7,824-note / ~234k-edge universe a pass takes minutes, so edits 2 and 3 both read "needed" and spawn again: up to 6 threads, each opening its own `Connection` (incoming) or hammering the shared `state.db` mutex per 500-row batch (outgoing). Three silent consequences. (a) `recompute_all_incoming` (links_backfill.rs:317) retries a busy window only 8×400 ms; with two peers writing, that budget is exceeded, `run` returns Err, and the ONLY report is `diag_log` to `.constellation/diagnostics.log` — "[incoming_links_backfill] FAILED (non-fatal)" — with nothing rescheduling until the next boot, so the incoming aggregates stay unstamped and every gated reader silently stays on the slow live path. (b) `links_backfill::run` shares ONE cursor row: a later thread does `read_cursor` and, because `version_current` is still false, does NOT reset it — it resumes at path P and never re-materialises rows [start..P] under the NEW vocabulary, while `outgoing_aggregate_assignments` (search.rs:2206) reads the LIVE registry snapshot per call. If that thread finalizes last it stamps the CURRENT fingerprint, `is_needed` goes false, and the rows before P keep aggregates (`outgoing_link_types`, `outgoing_top_rank`, the JSON) computed under the old vocabulary forever — wrong Base ordering and type breakdowns with no error anywhere. (c) Each spawn also mutates the SHARED writer connection's `busy_timeout` to 30 s (links_backfill.rs:149/171), so UI writes that would have failed fast now park for up to 30 s. `review_backfill.rs:30` already carries exactly the missing guard (`static RUNNING: AtomicBool` + `compare_exchange`, commented "threads racing on the same WAL — compare_exchange ensures exactly one runs"); the other eleven `maybe_schedule` modules do not.
confirmed_findings.reason:
CONFIRMED on the outgoing half only; the incoming and busy_timeout halves of the candidate are refuted.

Reachability verified: LinkTypesEditor.svelte:102-118 persists on every addType()/deleteType() with no debounce; link_types.rs:544-568 fires on_link_vocabulary_changed on any id-fingerprint change; search.rs:2750/2756 call both maybe_schedules, and neither has a run-slot guard (review_backfill.rs:30-49 has exactly the missing AtomicBool+compare_exchange). Both gate only on stamps written at completion (links_backfill.rs:447; incoming_links_backfill.rs:166), so edits during a multi-minute pass spawn additional full-corpus writers.

The surviving defect is links_backfill::run's conditional cursor reset (line 170). When version_current is false — a first-ever pass, a resumed interrupted pass, or a LINKS_OUTGOING_SCHEMA_VERSION bump — a thread spawned by a mid-run vocabulary edit does NOT reset the cursor; it reads it (line 176) and resumes at P. Rows [start..P] were materialised under the OLD vocabulary (outgoing_aggregate_assignments, search.rs:2205, regenerates its IN-list/rank CASE from the live registry per call, so pre-edit batches carry the old one) and are never revisited. Each thread stamps the fingerprint captured at its own start (line 160 -> line 464); the later-started thread carries the CURRENT fingerprint and, starting later from the same position at the same rate, is the one likely to finalize last. is_needed (line 87) then reads false forever, and the head rows keep old-vocabulary outgoing_link_types / _json / _top_rank permanently. Those columns have NO reader gate (unlike the incoming family) — they are served directly to Bases columns and sorting. Nothing is surfaced; diag_log records "completed".

The missing guard is exactly what breaks the heal: single-threaded, the pass would stamp the OLD fingerprint, is_needed would mismatch at the next boot, version_current would then be true, the cursor would reset, and every row would be re-materialised. Recovery now requires a later vocabulary edit or a user-initiated PJ-207 repair; derived_heal::maybe_schedule (derived_heal.rs:116-125) no-ops unless a crash marker is armed, and the boot reconcile does not converge on a clean pass.

Refuted parts: (a) both backfill connections set busy_timeout(30s) (links_backfill.rs:207, incoming_links_backfill.rs:127), so a peer's short autocommit UPDATE is absorbed by the busy handler rather than returned as an error, and even a genuine failure is correctness-preserving — no stamp means is_stamped stays false and every gated reader stays on the live getBacklinks path (incoming_links_backfill.rs:48-72), with a re-run at next boot. (b-incoming) recompute_all_incoming always walks the whole corpus from "", so a later thread rewrites every row under the new vocabulary — no stale head. (c) busy_timeout is per-connection wait behaviour, not a silent defect, and is unrelated to the race.

Fix: the review_backfill.rs:30 pattern (static RUNNING AtomicBool + compare_exchange) on links_backfill::maybe_schedule — and, for symmetry against wasted duplicate full-corpus passes, on incoming_links_backfill::maybe_schedule.

confirmed_findings.summary: linkMentionInNote rewrites a note's BODY on disk to insert a [[wikilink]] and refreshes only the main window's tabs — no `screen:note-saved`, so a second screen showing that note keeps rendering the un-linked text indefinitely.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: linkMentionInNote (store.ts:1612-1690) writes via writeNote(…, 'link_mention'), then calls reloadTabsFromDisk + reindexNote — both main-window-scoped — and never emits `screen:note-saved`. The write is gated, so watcher_suppress blocks the `library-changed` fallback. Scenario: note B is open on the second screen (e.g. pushed there, or opened from the SS Dashboard note list at SecondScreenPage.svelte:1390). In the main window the user opens B's Backlinks/Unlinked-mentions panel and clicks "link it" for a mention of A. Disk now has `[[A]]` in B's body. The second screen's model for B is clean and stale: it shows the plain-text mention, its cockpit re-fetch is keyed on path+reloadNonce (SecondScreenCockpit.svelte:99-110) and neither changes, so even the link graph beside it does not update. Same gap on the sibling closed-note writers that also skip the broadcast: addLinkToNote's closed branch (store.ts:1562, 'reviewer_connect') and addTagToNote's closed branch (src/routes/+layout.svelte:7079, 'add_tag').
confirmed_findings.reason: The mechanism is real and reachable, but the impact is smaller than claimed. VERIFIED: linkMentionInNote (src/lib/libraries/store.ts:1612-1672) writes B's body through gated writeNote(...,'link_mention') and then only main-window-scoped refreshes (reloadTabsFromDisk + reindexNote); it never emits 'screen:note-saved' (exhaustive grep: only store.ts:652/:1868/:6097 and secondScreen.ts:157 emit it). The Rust write_note (libraries.rs:889) routes through gate_write, which calls watcher_suppress::mark_with_parent (write_gate.rs:256-257), so the watcher's 'library-changed' — the second screen's only fallback (SecondScreenPage.svelte:780-796) — never fires. The SS's complete listener set (screen:note-saved u2 :673, cascade:rewrote :716, library-changed :780, note-created :803, index-repair:done :813) therefore never calls adoptFreshDiskIntoSS(:610) and never bumps cockpitReload, so an SS view of B renders the pre-link plain text indefinitely, with no surfaced error. Same gap on the sibling closed-note writers (store.ts:1562 'reviewer_connect'; +layout.svelte:7079 'add_tag'). REFUTED PORTIONS: (1) the klass 'index-divergence' is wrong — reindexNote is AWAITED at store.ts:1667, so SQLite stays consistent with disk; (2) the write is durable and a failure THROWS into BacklinksPanel.linkMention's catch -> reportSaveFailure (save-health banner + Retry), so no false success; (3) the stale SS model can never write back — ssReadOnly=true on every SS NoteEditor (SecondScreenPage.svelte:208, used at :1210/:1253/:1419) plus setDisplayOnlyWindow() (:213) which makes flushOutgoing a hard no-op (store.ts:688) — so the [[link]] cannot be reverted and no user work is lost; (4) the shared write-ahead net cannot resurrect the stale bytes either, because PJ-181's staleSnapshot gate (store.ts:3076-3077) prefers disk whenever a snapshot entry no longer matches it. Net: a genuine, silent, persistent display-vs-disk staleness in a read-only auxiliary window — the same class the G3 pass fixed for saves (HIGH #2) and cascades (HIGH #1) — but with no source-of-truth loss, no index divergence, no clobber path, no freeze and no leak. Proportionate fix: emit('screen:note-saved',{path}) after the write in all three closed/open writers (linkMentionInNote, addLinkToNote's closed branch, addTagToNote's closed branch), matching navFlushEnv's onSaved at store.ts:652.

confirmed_findings.summary: addTagToNote's CLOSED-note branch writes the note's frontmatter through the gate and reindexes, but never emits `screen:note-saved` — the open-note branch gets it for free via saveTabContent's runPostSave, so the two halves of one action behave differently across windows.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The open branch routes through saveTabContent, whose runPostSave emits `screen:note-saved` (store.ts:1868). The closed branch (+layout.svelte:7079) calls writeNote + reindexNote directly with no emit. "Closed in the main window" does not mean "not displayed": the second screen keeps its own openTabs and its own peek pane, so note A can be closed in main and open on the SS at the same time. Scenario: the user tags note A from the file-tree right-click / command palette while A is not open in main but IS the note on the second screen. The tag lands in A's frontmatter on disk and in note_meta; the gated write suppresses the watcher, so the SS is told nothing. The SS's NoteEditor keeps composing its display from a model whose frontmatter lacks the tag, and its Properties/Tags surfaces show the pre-tag state with no error. Because the SS is read-only the disk copy is safe, but the screen the user is reading from is silently wrong about the note's properties.
confirmed_findings.reason:
Real, reachable, and silent — but narrower in blast radius than the candidate claims.

Concrete failure: (1) On the second screen, open note A via the DashboardView note click (SecondScreenPage.svelte:1390, the SS's OWN openTabs store) or via the Sky View peek pane (loadPeekPreview, line 354) — both mount a real NoteEditor → NotePane → PropertyEditor rendering A's tags (NoteEditor.svelte:791). (2) A is NOT in the main window's openTabs. (3) In main, right-click A in the file tree → Add tag (or the batch tag action, +layout.svelte:10376/10385). (4) addTagToNote takes the closed branch at +layout.svelte:7079: writeNote + reindexNote, with no emit. (5) No signal reaches the SS by ANY channel — verified exhaustively: writeNote is a bare invoke (store.ts:2837); reindexNote is a bare invoke (store.ts:4027); write_note routes through gate_write, which calls watcher_suppress::mark_with_parent (write_gate.rs:256-257), and watcher.rs:119 filters those paths, so library-changed never fires; the Rust announce escape hatch (announce_disk_write / announce_frontmatter_writes) exists only in universe.rs:2630 and sources/mod.rs:685, never on write_note. The SS's only content-refresh channels are screen:note-saved (u2, line 673), library-changed (u5, line 780), cascade:rewrote (line 716) and ss-mutations — none fire. (6) The SS's PropertyEditor keeps showing A without the tag, and its flat note list / tag counts stay stale too (loadAllData is only armed by library-changed / note-created / index-repair:done). Nothing is surfaced: all three failure exits in addTagToNote write to templateActionError, but the success path has nothing to say. The divergence persists until an unrelated event touches that path.

The asymmetry is confirmed: the open branch gets the emit for free via saveTabContent's runPostSave (store.ts:1868); the closed branch has no equivalent. This is the same concern the 2026-08-01 inspection already accepted as real and fixed for the other two channels (u2's "SS never adopted main→SS saves", u5's external-edit routing) — this is the one remaining unannounced channel. It is also the ONLY bare `await writeNote(` in +layout.svelte, so the finding is specific, not a class.

Severity downgraded from MED to LOW: the candidate's klass "index-divergence" is wrong — the index does NOT diverge (reindexNote runs; note_meta/FTS are correct), and disk is correct. SecondScreenPage.svelte:208 is `const ssReadOnly = true;`, passed to all three NoteEditor mounts (1210/1253/1419), and NoteEditor hard-returns on readOnly at every write/rename site (208, 285, 361, 461, 541, 686), so the stale model can never write back. Impact is confined to a stale property row plus stale tag counts on one secondary read-only display, self-healing on the next save/cascade/external-edit adopt for that path. No knowledge, no disk state, and no index is at risk. Fix is one line: emit('screen:note-saved', { path }) after the reindexNote in the closed branch, matching runPostSave.

confirmed_findings.summary: `screen:ready` is emitted once, from the hidden second-screen webview's onMount at app boot, but main only starts listening for it inside handleToggleSecondScreen — so waitForScreenReady always burns its full 2000 ms timeout and the SS sits on its idle state for two seconds after every open.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: tauri.conf.json:21-28 creates the `second-screen` window at startup with `visible: false`; the webview still loads screen.html, so SecondScreenPage's onMount runs at boot and `await emitScreenReady()` (SecondScreenPage.svelte:956) fires its one and only `screen:ready` there. handleToggleSecondScreen (+layout.svelte:5859-5877) then does `await openSecondScreenSmart(); secondScreenOpen = true; await waitForScreenReady();` — waitForScreenReady (secondScreen.ts:380-390) registers a fresh listener for an event that already fired minutes earlier and will never fire again, so it resolves only via its `setTimeout(…, 2000)` fallback. Every time the user opens the second screen it shows its empty 'open a note in the main window' cockpit for a full 2 s before emitEditorPanels arrives, and the handler is parked on that await the whole time. Nothing surfaces the miss — the timeout path resolves rather than rejects, so the handshake reports success while having done nothing.
confirmed_findings.reason: Mechanism verified end-to-end in source, including the framework crates. (1) tauri.conf.json:20-28 declares `second-screen` with `visible: false` and no `create: false`; tauri-2.10.3 src/app.rs:2373 builds every config window at setup (`create` defaults true). (2) wry-0.54.2 src/webview2/mod.rs navigates the webview and only afterwards calls `controller.SetIsVisible(attributes.visible)` — a hidden webview still loads and runs its JS. So static/screen.html → src/screen-entry.ts mounts SecondScreenPage at app boot. (3) SecondScreenPage.svelte:652 onMount registers all listeners and calls `await emitScreenReady()` at :956 — the ONLY call site (grep: import at :54, emit at :956; no re-emit on show/focus). (4) The window is never destroyed: lib.rs:296-302 close_second_screen = `win.hide()`, and lib.rs:739-742 intercepts CloseRequested with `api.prevent_close(); window.hide()`. onMount therefore never runs again for the process lifetime. (5) secondScreen.ts:380-390 waitForScreenReady registers a FRESH `listen('screen:ready')` at call time and Tauri does not replay past events; its only callers are +layout.svelte:5863 (handleToggleSecondScreen) and :5887 (handleSendToSecondScreen), invoked minutes after the single boot-time emit. Result: every second-screen open burns the full `setTimeout(..., 2000)` fallback, and because the fallback resolves rather than rejects, the handshake reports success while having verified nothing — no error, no log, nothing surfaced. Corroborated by lab/reports/SESSION-LOG-2026-04-06.md:195, which shows this replaced a 600 ms setTimeout and was signed off on `npx vite build` clean only — never runtime-verified; it tripled the delay it was meant to remove. NOT an app-killer, and I refute any data-integrity reading: the SS `screen:editor-panels` listener has existed since boot, so the payload emitted after the wait is delivered and rendered intact; no disk write, no index/search.db path, no source-of-truth divergence. The `await` is a promise, not a blocked thread, so the main window stays responsive (no freeze); the timer always fires and `unsub` always runs (no leak); and the state self-corrects visibly within 2 s. Only real secondary effect: if the user toggles SS closed inside the 2 s window, the pending `emitEditorPanels({active:true})` lands on the now-hidden SS — display state only, consistent with Display-Not-Domain. Confirmed as a deterministic dead-handshake + 2 s latency defect, silent but non-destructive.

confirmed_findings.summary: sky_nodes.maturity is a time-thresholded value with no time-driven recompute: the only maintainers fire on a note save or a link change, so the 'canonical' (30-day) and 'wilting' (90-day) states are unreachable in steady state and Sky View permanently disagrees with every surface that computes maturity live.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: maturity_sql_expr (search.rs:266) reads days_since_modified / days_since_created against strftime('%s','now'). Its three maintainers are: note_meta_sky_maturity_au (line 5908, WHEN NEW.modified IS NOT OLD.modified OR NEW.created_at IS NOT OLD.created_at — i.e. only on a save, when days_since_modified is by definition 0, so it can never produce 'canonical' or 'wilting'), maintain_sky_after_save (search.rs:2670, which by design returns an empty affected set unless the note's targets/name/aliases changed), and recompute_after_link_status_change (archive/unarchive). Nothing recomputes on the passage of time. sky_backfill is one-shot behind schema_versions.sky; and since PJ-207 the boot reconcile (reconcile.rs::run) heals only EXISTENCE drift — converge_derived_views now runs ONLY from derived_heal when a crash marker is armed (derived_heal.rs:markers_armed) or from an explicit 'Repair now'. Concrete case: note 'Attention' accumulates 12 inbound links on 1 June, is last edited 1 June, and receives no further links. Its stored maturity is written once as 'evergreen'. On 5 July it satisfies canonical (inbound ≥ 10, untouched ≥ 30 days) but sky_nodes.maturity still reads 'evergreen' forever. Sky View reads the stored column (cache.rs:1028 read_sky_nodes_raw_in_schema, `SELECT … stratum, maturity … FROM sky_nodes`), while the Reviewer computes it live (review.rs:963 maturity_label → maturity::compute_state) and the 360 Inspector and Map do the same. So two surfaces label the same note differently, permanently, with no error — directly violating the 'surfaces agree' invariant that maturity_sql_expr's own doc-comment (search.rs:266-290) states as its contract.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified by reading every link in the chain. maturity_sql_expr (search.rs:266-322) thresholds on strftime('%s','now') (canonical >=30d, wilting >=90d since modified), but no maintainer of sky_nodes.maturity is driven by time: note_meta_sky_maturity_au (search.rs:5908) fires only when modified/created_at change; maintain_sky_after_save (search.rs:2670) recomputes only sky_affected_paths, empty unless targets/name/aliases changed; sky_backfill (sky_backfill.rs:395) is `WHERE maturity IS NULL` behind schema_versions.sky, one-shot per row. The only full refresh, recompute_all_sky, reaches solely from converge's after_repair_run (search.rs:12075, the explicit repair walk), heal_interrupted_walk, after_mig108, after_vocabulary_change and after_incoming_backfill; derived_heal::maybe_schedule is markers_armed-gated and its own doc says it is a "no-op ... every ordinary launch" (derived_heal.rs:116-123). The boot reconcile (reconcile.rs:256) heals existence drift only and calls no converge. Sky View reads the STORED column (cache.rs:1026 SELECT ... maturity FROM sky_nodes -> cache_boot_snapshot_sky -> +layout.svelte:1169 skyNodes -> graphEngine.ts:2222 ring + legend), and the live-compute enrichment cannot rescue it: enrichNodesBackground has exactly one caller (+layout.svelte:9005 onRequestEnrichment), reachable only from GraphMindView's empty-legend button (GraphMindView.svelte:1307-1327), which never renders once sky_nodes is back-filled. Meanwhile the file-tree/tab dots (maturityMap <- compute_note_maturity, maturity.rs:38, live) and the Reviewer (review.rs:963) compute live and are re-scanned (PJ-207 section 11, +layout.svelte:6154). Concrete reachable case: a note with 12 inbound links last edited 1 June gets 'evergreen' stored; on 1 July every live surface says 'canonical' (amber) while Sky View still rings it evergreen-green and buckets it under the wrong legend name, permanently, with no error and no drift notice (PJ-207's check compares .md mtimes to note_meta and cannot see a derived column stale against its own formula). One correction to the candidate: canonical/wilting are not unreachable - sky_backfill and maintain_sky_after_save can both produce them - the real defect is that the value never advances with the passage of time once written. Downgraded to LOW: nothing on disk or in note_meta is lost or corrupted, the column is fully recomputable, the correct value remains visible on the Reviewer and file tree, and the existing Repair door converges it - this is derived-display staleness, not the knowledge/index-loss class.

confirmed_findings.summary: `record_change` returns silently when `state.db` is None (`let Some(conn) = guard.as_ref() else { return }`), and its caller `record_shape_change` (shape.rs:342) still returns `Ok(())` — the shape transition is written to the note on disk but no `shape_history` row exists, and the frontend's `.catch()` can never fire.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: During the cold-boot init window (or the seconds after a universe switch, when `invalidate_search_state` has set `db = None`), the user opens a note and picks ⋯ → Shape → Page. `NoteEditor.applyShape` writes `shape: page` into the note through the model's own durable save (NoteEditor.svelte:580 — pure disk, no DB), then fires `invoke('record_shape_change', …)` (NoteEditor.svelte:605). `record_change` takes the lock, finds None at shape.rs:239, returns; `record_shape_change` returns Ok(()) at shape.rs:342; the `.catch(console.error)` never runs. Nothing anywhere records that the step was lost. Later the user picks ⋯ → Revert shape: `undo_shape` (shape.rs:369) selects the newest `undone = 0` row — which is now an OLDER change — marks it consumed and hands back ITS `from_shape`, and `applyShape(target, false)` writes that stale value into the note's frontmatter. The user's `.md` silently acquires a shape from two changes ago, the change they actually made can never be undone, and the redo-branch truncation (`DELETE … WHERE undone = 1`, shape.rs:247) was also skipped so the history is left non-linear. If no earlier row exists at all the user instead gets "Nothing to undo" for a change they just made.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real and reachable, but materially smaller than claimed. Verified: `record_change` (shape.rs:227-256) silently returns on `guard.as_ref()` None at :239, and `record_shape_change` returns Ok(()) at :342 regardless. `state.db` is genuinely None in two windows — the cold-boot init (ensure_search_db_ready, search.rs:11440+, documented 20-40s, `db` stored only after init_db returns) and after `invalidate_search_state` (search.rs:11212) on a universe switch — and nothing gates the shape controls on search readiness (NotePane.svelte:1599-1617 gates only on `readOnly`), so a restored tab's ⋯ → Shape → Page is clickable in that window. The disk write does land (NoteEditor.applyShape:548-587, model → compose → saveNoteSession('shape_set'), no DB), the history row does not, and the redo truncation (:247) is skipped. A later `undo_shape` (:371-378) then returns an OLDER row's `from_shape`, which `applyShape(target, false)` writes into the note. The `.catch(console.error)` is invisible in release (devtools disabled), so no error reaches the user. WHY NOT MED/HIGH: the source of truth is correct — the `.md` gets the shape the user chose; only the auxiliary undo stack diverges. The payload is a closed two-value presentation vocabulary (SHAPES = ["scrap","page"], :45) that by design "governs how a note is PRESENTED... never what it CONTAINS" (:38-44) — no body, content, link or index data is touched, and the file stays byte-exact otherwise (revert_to_unshaped_restores_original_bytes, :544). The wrong revert is visible on screen and in Properties and is one click to re-set. The module itself treats shape_history as discardable, not a record of truth: the v1→v2 upgrade does an unconditional `DELETE FROM shape_history` (:106) reasoning "the notes' actual shapes live in the files." Note also that returning Err from record_change would NOT fix this — the caller ignores errors deliberately ("losing a history row must not fail the edit", NoteEditor.svelte:596-609); the real fix is either recording through a path that waits for DB readiness or surfacing "shape history unavailable" in the UI.
